contexts.text: The influx from the Divine passes (down) into use, and there ceases.
The Sensuous is the ultimate of man's life... for (all the interior things) cease in it, and thus quiesce upon it. Example.
For everything spiritual ceases in that which is called natural truth; and everything celestial in that which is called natural good; and there they subsist.
The Divine truth ... in an external form in which the interior things cease. Signification, Explanation.
For that which is outermost not only contains the interior things; but they also cease in it...
As man's interiors cease in the flesh and bones ... so the Word must have an ultimate in which its interiors may cease...
That the interiors of the Church, of worship, and of the Word, cease in their external, and rest upon it...
The senses, speech, and actions ... are the ultimates in which the Divine influx ceases...
The terraqueous globe ... is the ultimate work, in which all things cease...
That the atmospheres ... in their ultimates cease in substances and matters... Explanation.
